notes.text: Trivial wrapper: func_8026EDD0(&D_800F1F20). Only diff is instruction order within the same prologue: target does addiu sp,-0x18 FIRST, then lui/addiu a0 (arg loading) then sw $ra; my gcc-2.7.2-kmc -O2 build emits stack adjust, then sw $ra, then lui/addiu. Also target has a `nop` after jal (jal before addiu a0 is inverted) - looks like scheduling difference. Tried: pointer locals, u8 D_800F1F20 as global array (that gives lui+addiu, correct operands). Not matched; possible the whole file was built with slightly different scheduling flags. Everything else identical.

Best 2520 (38.5%). BEST SOURCE: s32 func_80273E60(s16 arg0, s32 arg1, s32 arg2, s32 arg3, s32 arg4, s32 arg5, s32 arg6) { s16 v = arg0; if (D_800D7908 == 0) { if (v != -1) { if (v >= 0x7530) { func_802701C4(D_800F1F20, v, arg5); return -1; } return func_8026F7BC(D_800F1F20, v, arg1, arg2, arg3, arg4, arg5, arg6); } } return -1; } with s32 func_8026F7BC(void*, s16, s32, s32, s32, s32, s32, s32).
Missing piece: the target's argument marshalling reads its own incoming home slots back (lw v0,0x38 -> sw 0x14, lw v0,0x40 -> sw 0x1c, lw v0,0x34 -> sw 0x10, lw a2,0x2c, lw a3,0x30) and spills a2/a1/a3 there early. That only happens if those values are re-loaded from memory in the source, e.g. the args arrive as different types or are passed via a second level (the original may have taken arg1..arg3 as struct/other types so they got spilled). With flattened params gcc keeps them in t-registers instead. Tried early-return, goto, r temp, condition inversion: all worse or equal.

Best 230 (79%). Source: s32 func_80405230(s32 arg0, s32 arg1, s32 arg2) { func_80403D34(arg2, D_414F00); return 1; } with `s32 func_80403D34(s32, u8*)` and `extern u8 D_414F00[]`. Target: `move $a0,$a2` BEFORE `lui/addiu $a2,%hi/lo(D_414F00)` and before `sw $ra`; mine emits sw $ra then address then move. Also target's address goes into a2 (mine a1) — because of the pre-move of a2->a0 the address can go to a2. Tried: local u8 *p = D_414F00 before the call, `s32 r = func(...); return r?1:1` — no change. Maybe source is `return func_80403D34(arg2, D_414F00), 1;` or the call's prototype differs (arg2 passed as void*), or the helper's 2nd param is `u8*` const.

Best 60 (95.3%). Source: s32 func_80405288(S804 *arg0) { if (!(D_800D77D4 & 0xF80007FF)) { arg0->unk8 &= ~0x40000; } return 0; } . Only diff: target loads the constant mask into v1 (`lui $v1,0xf800`) before the global load; mine emits `lui v0,%hi/lw` first then `lui v1,0xf800`. Tried writing the mask as a local `s32 m = 0xF80007FF;` — no effect. Suggest writing the test as `if ((D_800D77D4 & 0xF80007FF) == 0)` or reorder expressions (e.g. `0xF80007FF & D_800D77D4`); might hoist the constant. Callee of func_80406C30 (that one's variant uses 0x100 & D_800D77D0).

Best 430 (81.3%). Source: S804 {s32 unk0..unk14}; func_80405170(S804 *arg0) { s32 idx = D_800D77E6; s32 t = ((s32*)((u8*)arg0->unk14))[idx]; idx = func_8040348C(); func_802A08B8(t + (idx - 3), D_800BC470, D_800CE200); return 0; }
Diff: target after `jal func_8040348C` does `nop; addiu v0,v0,-3` (result adjusted in place in v0, then `addu a0,s0,v0`), and materialises a1 (D_800BC470) address before a2 (D_800CE200 lw). Mine does `addiu s0,s0,-3` and the a1/a2 address setup in the other order, plus `move v0,zero` placed before the ra restore (mine after). Try: `s32 off = func_8040348C(); func_802A08B8(t + off - 3, ...)` with two separate locals, and assignments that keep the returned value in v0; also try declaring the a2 load before a1 (e.g. write `func_802A08B8(t + off + (-3), D_800BC470, D_800CE200)` where the -3 is folded). Note the array index is u8 D_800D77E6 (sll by 2).

Trivial getter, but the target puts the load in the jr delay slot (lui; lw; jr; nop); GCC and IDO 7.1 both emit lui; jr; lw; nop after any variant tried. Can't get closer with C under the project's compiler.
Setter D_800F2054 = arg0; target: lui at; sw; jr; nop (store in delay slot). GCC/IDO always put jr first — pure schedule difference, no C fix found; retry under another compiler.

14 insns, best score 60. Only diff: target emits `move v1,a0` before the `lui/lw v0,D_800D7908` global test; gcc-2.7.2-kmc issues the global load first. Real code: if (D_800D7908 == 0) func_802701C4(&D_800F1F20, arg0, arg1);

Best 1254 with: if (D_800D7908 != 0) return -1; then n=0; temp_s1=func_802706E0(&D_800F1F20); func_802706D8(&D_800F1F20,1); temp_s0=func_8026FD24(&D_800F1F20, arg0, *(s32*)&zero, *(s32*)&zero, *(s32*)&zero, n, arg1); func_802706D8(&D_800F1F20,temp_s1); return temp_s0; with f32 zero=0.0f and func_8026FD24 proto (s32*,s32,s32,s32,s32,s32,s32). Key insight: the three float 0.0 args are passed in STACK slots 0x20/0x24/0x28 (real float params, stored as mtc1/swc1), and func_8026FD24 takes 7 args with a0,a1 explicit, so its sp+0x10 slot holds param 5 — target reloads lw a2/a3 from 0x20/0x24 and lw v0 from 0x28 into sp+0x10 AFTER building a0/a1. Remaining: prologue size, arg-build order (need float spills emitted before the first call and the lw's after moves), which this GCC orders differently. Likely another compiler (see func_80274114 notes).

Best 385. Target order: prologue saves s0/s1 (s0=a0,s1=a1); lw v0,0x14(s0); lw a3,0x20(v0) [a3 because a0/a1/a2 already set by preceding insns: a0=4 and a1=0 constants come before jal in a1's slot]; jal D_80242160 with (4, 0, *(s32*)(*(s32**)(arg0+0x14)+0x20)); then &D_800CCA80/a1=s0/a2=1 jal D_80203F74; sw zero,0xcc(s1); a0=s0, a1=1 jal D_8021B7EC with a2=a0. Tried: m2c order (90), statements reordered with arg1->unkCC volatile-ish (385/614), assigning args to locals first, D_80203F74 s32 vs void returns. Remaining trouble: compiler schedules loads/lui late and merges the 0xCC store into the last block; also sp size 0x18 vs 0x20. Suspect real source is one call per statement where D_80242160's 2nd/3rd args are constants 4/0 and the value loaded earlier into a temp.

Best 270. Target: if (p->unk28 != 0) return p->unk48; else return 0; — but ROM emits the NULL path as a separate 'jr $ra / move $v0,$zero' block after the taken branch (beqz to 0x20 with a nop delay slot), i.e. a void-ish block with its own return, 10 insns. My code (both ternary/if-else and early return) gives 8 insns: 'beqz / move v0,zero' in delay slot and a single jr. So the original likely isn't an if/else return: perhaps a static helper returning via a variable or a struct returning s32 from a function whose body ends with the two returns in a different order. Try: 'if (p->unk28) {...}; ' with the assignment to a global result, or restructure as do{...}while(0). Don't repeat plain if/else/ternary.

Best 160 (68%). Target is 5 insns: 'addiu v0,zero,1; lui at,hi; sw v0,lo; jr $ra; nop' — i.e. the store is scheduled AFTER... no: store happens before jr but there's a trailing nop instead of 'addiu v0,zero,1' in the delay slot. My code always emits 4 insns: addiu/lui/sw/jr with the jr last (no nop) — identical prefix but one insn fewer. Something forces a 'jr/nop' epilogue rather than 'jr' plus delay slot fill, e.g. two separate stores or a return path that doesn't set v0 (so the addiu cannot go in the delay slot). Try: return value assigned via a different expression so v0 is live at jr, and consider the function being 's32 f(void){ D=1; }' compiled as ... Actually with void return gcc still emits 4. Try: 'if (1) {D_800B3630 = 1;}' or a global written via a local temp plus early return before it.

Only diff left is a trailing `nop` after `jr $ra` that the ROM has and my build cannot emit: the ROM's endlabel includes 4 bytes of padding (the function runs into padding). This "function" is two functions merged: 0x8028E738 (124-0x74=0x50 bytes, ends after `jr $ra; move $v0,$a0` at 0x8028E778) and a second one at 0x8028E77C that also reads D_800B3628: `if (w28 == 0) return 1; else return !(f24 < f10)` (bc1fl skips the clear). Suggest split_function at 0x8028E77C. Best C for first part (score 1305): extern struct ptr D_800B3628, struct {pad0x10; f32 f10; pad; f32 f20 at 0x20; f32 f24 at 0x24; s32 w28 at 0x28}; `s32 r=0; if (o->w28) { if (!(o->f10 < o->f20)) { if (!(o->f24 < o->f10)) r=1; } } return r;` gives the right instruction sequence; remaining diffs are register/branch-offset placement (target uses bc1tl for the second test, needs the second comparison as the last statement of the block).

Merged function: at 0x8028E9D8 `D_800B3630 = 0; return;` (8 bytes), then a getter at 0x8028E9E0 `return D_800B3630;`, then at 0x8028E9E8 a function like func_8028E738 but with `(o->w30 & 2) != 0`. Suggest split_function at 0x8028E9E0 and 0x8028E9E8.

Free-slot allocator. Globals: D_800F6008 is a u16 pair {cur at 0x0, limit at 0x2}; D_800F5F92 and D_800F5F93 are u8 arrays of 0x18*4-byte rows; D_800F5C43 is a struct array with stride 0x10 whose byte 0 is freed. Algorithm: idx = cur++; if ((s16)cur >= 0x18) cur = limit; then for each of the two arrays (D_800F5F92 then D_800F5F93) if arr[idx*4] != 0xFF { D_800F5C43[arr[idx*4]*0x10].b0 = 0xFF; arr[idx*4] = 0xFF; } return idx. Best score 3060. Key hints from diffs: the target uses `lui $at, %hi(X); addu $at,$at,$v1; lbu %lo(X)($at)` — that is indexed addressing through a *constant base* (like `D_800F5F92[idx*4]` with D_800F5F92 declared as a byte array at a known symbol), and `lhu $a0, ($v1)` / `lhu 2($v1)` show the fl->cur/limit accesses go through one base register (declaring `extern FreeList D_800F6008` gets the first, but the +2 load must be `fl->limit`, not `*(u16*)((u8*)&D_800F6008+2)` — the latter emits a second lui). The ROM re-reads arr[idx*4] twice (once for the compare, once for the *0x10 index), so write the source as `if (D_800F5F92[idx*4] != 0xFF) { D_800F5C43[(s32)D_800F5F92[idx*4]*0x10] = ...; D_800F5F92[idx*4] = 0xFF; }` with plain indexing, not a cached byte in a temp. ROM values idx before the limit check (the sll $v0,$a0,16 sits in the branch-delay slot of bnez), which copying from a u16 local at once gives. Keep trying: I ran out of budget.

See previous note: wrapper around func_8026349C. Target frame -0x38; builds incoming stack words at 0x10/0x14 (from 0x48/0x4C), 0x18/0x1C (from 0x50/0x54), constants 1,1,0x80000 at 0x20/0x24/0x28, and spills/reloads $a3 at 0x44. Best 1157 with `void f(s32,s32,s32,s32,const s32*);` + local `s32 a[3]={...}`; passing 10 scalars also 1157. Tried: 6 scalars + S-param {1,1,0x80000} (1624, tail-copies the struct instead of filling the outgoing slot), pointer-to-array (1424). The target loads the two incoming stack pairs into $v1/$t0 and stores them in the outgoing area itself, and reloads a3 from 0x44 before the call — so the source probably passes 4 stack scalars through plus something that makes gcc spill a3 (e.g. the 4th arg is also used after the args are evaluated). Also note score 0 needs the -0x38 frame: the extra 8 bytes vs mine come from the a3 save slot at 0x44 (beyond the frame), reachable only via that spill.

Target: `lw $v0,0x154($a1); jr $ra; nop`. Two very different C forms both give a body that is `jr $ra; lw $v0,0x154($a1); nop` (jr first!) — score 160 — while the unused-load form gives no load at all (score 100). Since even a plain `return *(s32*)((u8*)arg1+0x154)` produces jr-before-lw, this looks like a boundary/offset quirk of this tiny 12-byte function (likely the real body ends at jr and the `nop` is padding; the lw may belong before the jr but the tool aligns differently), or the function begins mid-padding. Suggest report_boundary / check whether the function really starts at 0x8024C0F4. Register/operand were always right.

Score 30, all matching except 3 stores: target writes pD8 at 0xD8, f158 at 0x158, f15C at 0x15C; mine land at 0xD4/0x154/0x158, i.e. exactly 4 bytes early - my struct has one too few bytes before offset 0xD8 (so my pD8 sits at 0xD4... actually the p28/pC4/pD0 stores matched, so the first too-early one is pD8). My layout: p28@0x28, pC4@0xC4, pD0@0xD0, pD8@0xD8, f158@0x158, f15C@0x15C - the pad0_4[0x154-0xDC] should be fine... The compiler placed pD8 4 bytes early, so my struct offsets must be recomputed: use EXPICIT absolute addressing `*(void **)((u8*)arg1+0xD8) = &D_24BDF8;` etc. That is the obvious next step (byte-arith stores). Note the order target emits: p28, pC4, pD0, then move a2,zero, pD8, f158=0, jal, f15C=0 (f15C after the call arg setup).

Best 720 (m2c-ish, |&D_800F4AC8!=NULL|&&|*p==1| in one condition), my structured version 877. Key observed diffs and hints: (1) target reloads D_800F4AC8 twice more (after the first NULL check: `lui/lw v0,%hi/lo(D_800F4AC8)`, then `lbu v1,($v0)`), i.e. the source uses the global D_800F4AC8 directly each time, not a cached local pointer (my `p` local collapses the loads; my versions with p==target-cached g0 got s0 but then call args became wrong order). (2) target passes the float as lui 0x41cc/ori 0xcccc = 25.5f written as 0x41CCCCCC? no: 0x41CCCCCC is 25.600000381; gcc emitted 0x41cccc when I wrote 25.5f, so the literal is NOT 25.5f; 0x41CCCCCC means value 25.599999..., likely written as 25.6f but that gave ori 0xcccd (rounding). So write the bits: use `*(f32*)&(u32){0x41CCCCCC}`-style or a union/constant trick to get 0x41cccc. (3) target arg order in D_8024220C: `lw a0,(s0)` [global], `addiu a2,sp,0x18` [buf, third arg], `jal`, `addiu a1,a0,0x168` - so a1 = a0+0x168 computed AFTER jal (delay slot style) - comes naturally from f(g, g+0x168, buf). (4) Register saves: target uses s0=D_800F4AC8 address, s1=a0, s2=a1 and saves s1,s2,ra,s0 in that order; my code saved s1,s2,ra,s0 differently, need a temp like `u8 *g = D_800F4AC8;` used only in the *p check but always reloaded... probably: `if (D_800F4AC8) { if (D_800F4AC8->? == 1) ... }` with the address in s0. (5) Target buffer at sp+0x18, args 0x10/0x14 for args 5/6. Also need declaration `Obj` (offsets 0x28/0xC4/0xD0/0xD8/0x154/0x158/0x15C from func_8024C108) - don't trust it, my struct gave 4-byte-early stores in func_8024C108, so arithmetic byte offsets may be needed. Best saved attempt is the structured one.

Best 1220 (unchanged from autopilot draft). Target structure: n=0; lim = D_800AA304/(x+x) + D_800AA304 (note: adds LIMIT first in float then the loop compares (f32)(1<<n) < lim); if (D_800AA300 <= x) return n; if (D_800AA304 < lim) do n++ while ((f32)(1<<n) < lim); return n. Key remaining problem: target loads D_800AA300 FIRST (for the compare) even though the arithmetic uses D_800AA304 first, i.e. the C compare/test comes first in source (early-return pattern: if (x >= D_800AA300) return 0; is emitted with c.le.s before the div because gcc hoists the compare? target does `move v1,0; add.s f0,f12,f12; lwc1 f1,D_800AA300; lwc1 f2,D_800AA304; c.le.s f1,f12; div.s f0,f2,f0; bc1f; add.s f1,f0,f2; jr ra; move v0,v1` - so the source likely is:
  s32 n = 0; f32 lim = ...; if (x >= D_800AA300) return n; ...
with the compare written using D_800AA300 and the early return shared with the final return (both `return n` -> single return via v1). My versions emit div before the c.le.s because I compute lim in a separate statement/declaration - try `if (D_800AA300 <= x) return 0;` after a non-initialised lim, or use x>= vs <= sign to keep c.le.s. Also extra `nop`s after div/bc1f in mine come from the float compare scheduling - the target's if(D_800AA304 < lim) uses c.lt.s f2,f1 (k < lim, operand order matters: my c.lt.s f4,f2 wrong). Loop: `sllv v0,a0,v1` with a0=1 => 1<<n; mtc1/cvt from int; bc1tl with addiu v1,v1,1 in delay slot => do/while with n++ then test (f32)(1<<n) < lim but the increment must be the post-increment of the while condition — write `n++` inside body and `while ((f32)(1 << n) < lim)`, which gave right shape.

Can't get closer: the target is `lw v0,0xC(a0); jr ra; nop` and plain `return ((s32*)arg0)[3];` compiles to `lw v0,0xc($a0); jr $ra` (no nop, load already in the delay slot) at 160. The extra nop means gcc scheduled the load one step earlier in the ROM but there is no C that prevents delay-slot filling for a single load — no source-level lever here. Matching requires the ROM's exact 3-insn listing; every C variant tried (pointer indexing, byte offset, with a dummy global op) gives 2 or 10 insns. Only the plain 2-insn version is plausible original code.

Bitstream reader: off = base + width*arg1; idx = (off & 0xF0000000) | ((off & 0xFFFFFE0) >> 3); bit = off & 0x1F; word = idx[0] >> bit | idx[1] << (32-bit) if bit; mask to width bits when width<32. Best 445 (30 insns vs 29). Remaining diffs are scheduling of the mult/mflo and the base load: ROM orders `mult; lw base; mflo` then `addu`, and loads idx[0] AFTER computing bit; mine hoists the load. Also the delay-slot before `sltiu` differs (ROM `addiu v0,zero,1` in slot, mine nop) and the shift temp uses v0 vs a1. Try writing the read as inline expression `(p[0] >> bit) | (p[1] << (0x20 - bit))` with a temp for `0x20-bit` and separate `u32 lo = p[0]; u32 hi = p[1];` after the andi, or reversing the declaration order (t before w) to fix mflo/a3 vs a1.

Varargs-style arg spill: ROM is `lw v0,0x14(sp)` FIRST, then `sw a2,8(sp); sw a3,0xC(sp)` (a2/a3 homed by a normal prototype), then `sw a1,0(a0); lw v1,8(sp); lw t0,0xC(sp); lw t1,0x10(sp); sw...; jr; sw v0,0x10(a0)` (no v0=0, store in delay slot).
